title: Exam Week
subtitle: Ten weeks, one paper. This is the practice run, and it is meant to be long.
objectives: Recall the ten Science topics of the term
Use retrieval practice instead of re-reading
Name the traps that cost the most marks
Read an exam question properly before answering

cards.title: Everything from week 1 is back on the table
cards.text: Ten weeks, from the skeleton to distillation. The good news is that you have already learned all of it once.

cards.title: Ten weeks, one tap each
cards.text: This is your revision sheet. The second line of each is the mistake that costs the mark.

cards.title: Testing yourself beats reading it again
cards.text: Re-reading feels productive because the page looks familiar. Familiar is not the same as remembered.
points: **Close the notes.** Say the answer out loud.
**It feels harder** than reading, and it works better.
**The struggle is the part** that does the work.

question.text: Which revision method actually builds memory?
options: Closing the book and trying to recall the answer
question.explain: Retrieval practice. It feels harder than re-reading, and that difficulty is what makes it work.

cards.title: Watching a playthrough is not practice
cards.text: You can watch someone clear a boss ten times and still lose to it. The controller has to be in your hands.

cards.title: Four short sessions beat one long one
cards.text: The same total time, split across four days, produces more memory than one block the night before.
points: **Cramming works for a day**, then goes.

question.text: One long revision session is better than the same time split across several days.
question.explain: Spacing wins. Forgetting a little between sessions is what makes reloading it strengthen the memory.

cards.title: Good place to pause
cards.text: Part 2 is exam-room technique. The paper itself comes after that, and it is 24 questions.

cards.title: Most lost marks are not lost to not knowing
cards.text: They are lost to answering a question that was not asked. The reading is a skill of its own.

cards.title: Find the command word first
cards.text: Name, describe and explain want three different things. Answering the wrong one loses the mark even when the science is right.

cards.title: Answering the wrong question is swinging at nothing
cards.text: The effort is real and it lands nowhere. Reading the question twice costs five seconds and saves the mark.
points: **Read it again for the command word.**
**Five seconds.** It is the cheapest habit here.

cards.title: Never leave a multiple choice blank
cards.text: A blank scores zero for certain. A guess after crossing out two wrong options is far better than that.
points: **Mark it and move on** if it is slow.
**Come back at the end**, not now.

question.text: What should you do with a question you cannot answer straight away?
options: Mark it, move on, and come back at the end
Stay on it until it comes to you
Leave it blank and forget it
question.explain: Time spent stuck is time taken from questions you can do. Come back with whatever is left.

cards.title: Sleep is revision, not time off it
cards.text: Memory is filed overnight. An hour of sleep before the exam is usually worth more than an hour of cramming.
points: **Eat something.** The brain runs on glucose.

question.text: Staying up late to revise is a good trade the night before an exam.
question.explain: Memories are consolidated during sleep. Losing that usually costs more than the extra hour gains.

cards.title: The four that matter
points: **Test yourself.** Re-reading only feels like work.
**Space it out.** Four short beats one long.

quiz.text: How do muscles move a bone?
options: They pull in pairs; one pulls while the other relaxes
One pushes and the other pulls
quiz.explain: Week 1. Muscles only pull. Straightening your arm is the triceps pulling, not the biceps pushing.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: Which connects a muscle to a bone?
quiz.explain: Week 1. A ligament connects bone to bone; a tendon connects muscle to bone.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: Where are most nutrients absorbed?
quiz.explain: Week 2. The stomach breaks food down. Absorption happens in the small intestine.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: The large intestine is called large because it is longer than the small intestine.
quiz.explain: Week 2. It is wider but much shorter. The names refer to diameter.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: How does sweating cool the body?
options: It evaporates from the skin and carries heat away
It is cold when it leaves the body
quiz.explain: Week 3. Wiping sweat away removes the cooling before it can happen.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: What happens to the diaphragm when you breathe in?
options: It flattens and moves down, so chest pressure drops
It rises into a dome and pushes air in
It stays still while the ribs do the work
quiz.explain: Week 4. You do not suck air in. Pressure falls and the atmosphere pushes air down.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: Where does gas exchange happen?
options: All the way down the airway
quiz.explain: Week 4. Everything above the alveoli is plumbing that carries air.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: What do arteries have in common?
options: They carry blood away from the heart
They have valves along their length
quiz.explain: Week 5. The pulmonary artery carries oxygen-poor blood, which is why the definition is direction.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: A reflex is a very fast decision made by the brain.
quiz.explain: Week 5. The spinal cord handles it. The brain finds out afterwards.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: Roughly what share of animal species have no backbone?
quiz.explain: Week 6. Vertebrates are the small minority, and arthropods alone outnumber them many times over.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: Which mammals lay eggs?
quiz.explain: Week 6. They are still mammals, which is why the class is not defined by live birth.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: What is the difference between pollination and fertilisation?
options: Pollination is pollen arriving; fertilisation is the cells joining
They are two words for the same event
quiz.explain: Week 7. Arrival then joining. The exam separates them almost every year.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: What does the ovary of a flower become?
quiz.explain: Week 7. The ovules become the seeds; the ovary around them becomes the fruit.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: Why does variation matter?
options: It removes the need for parents
quiz.explain: Week 7. Clones are not stronger for being identical. One threat can take all of them.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: What separates a suspension from a colloid?
options: A suspension settles on standing; a colloid does not
A suspension is cloudy and a colloid is clear
A colloid is a pure substance
A suspension passes through filter paper
quiz.explain: Week 8. Cloudiness is not the test. Milk is cloudy and does not settle, so it is a colloid.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: What does the Tyndall effect show?
options: A beam scatters in a colloid but passes through a solution
A mixture is a pure substance
quiz.explain: Week 8. It tells colloids and solutions apart in seconds.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: Nothing has chemically reacted in a mixture.
quiz.explain: Week 8. Each part keeps its own properties, which is why mixtures can be separated physically.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: In salt water, which is the solvent?
quiz.explain: Week 9. The solute dissolves; the solvent does the dissolving.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: What does saturated mean?
options: No more will dissolve at that temperature
quiz.explain: Week 9. It is a limit, not a strength. Concentrated is the word for strong.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: Why do warm fizzy drinks go flat faster?
options: Gases become less soluble as temperature rises
Gases become more soluble as temperature rises
quiz.explain: Week 9. Heating dissolves more of most solids but less gas. That exception is examinable.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: How would you get pure water out of salt water?
quiz.explain: Week 10. Distillation keeps the liquid. Evaporation would leave the salt and lose the water.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: Filtering can separate salt from a salt solution.
quiz.explain: Week 10. Filtering only catches undissolved solids. A solution passes straight through.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: A solution has 5 g of solute in 100 g of solution. What is the concentration?
quiz.explain: Week 10. Concentration is solute divided by the whole solution, not by the solvent.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

quiz.text: What does boiling water actually do to make it safe?
options: Kills microbes; dissolved substances stay behind
quiz.explain: Week 10. Boiling is a biological fix, not a chemical one.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Science topics of the term

teacher.summary: Week 11 is exam week. The deck deliberately teaches no new Science: it is half revision method and half exam technique, both of which are the actual bottleneck at this stage. The two study claims are the best-evidenced findings in the field — retrieval practice beats re-reading, and spaced sessions beat one block — and they are given with the reason rather than as instructions. The figure is the real artifact here: ten taps, each giving the week's core fact and the specific error that loses the mark, mined from the misconception list of every lesson this term. The quiz is a full 24-question mixed paper covering all ten weeks, and the deck warns him of its length in advance rather than surprising him with it.
discussion: Ask him to say what each of the ten weeks covered before he opens the figure. What is missing is the revision list.
Ask what the difference is between name, describe and explain in a question.
Ask him which three traps on the map he would most likely fall for.
After the paper, look only at the missed questions. The score is not the useful part.
teacher.extension: Have him re-sit the paper two days later without revising in between. The gap is the point, and the second score is usually the honest one.
misconceptions: 'Re-reading notes is revising.' It builds familiarity, not recall. Closing the book is what works.
'Cramming the night before is efficient.' It holds for about a day. Spaced sessions hold for the exam.
'A blank answer is safer than a guess.' A blank scores zero for certain.
'Sleep is time taken away from revision.' Memory is consolidated overnight, so the trade usually loses.
